opening_line: The "just call my cell" excuse in your redesign checklist is the moment a site stops matching the business behind it. How many of your redesigns start with that exact conversation?
A logo as the invitation and the website as the room people walk into is a clean way to explain why one without the other falls flat. Do clients usually come to you with the logo already done?

You wrote that ecommerce builds aren't something you advertise, and Elo Coffee got the yes because it was the right fit. Turning down work that doesn't fit is how a small studio keeps its quality where it is.

Well-built versus poorly built, not custom versus WordPress, is the answer a lot of service owners need before someone pitches them a Next.js rebuild. Are clients showing up already half sold on that pitch?

Your point that residents open a municipal site to pay a utility bill or check garbage day, not to learn about the brand, changes where the design starts. Do you plan those sites around tasks from the first wireframe?

Your point about publishing better evidence, not more pages, now that AI makes pages cheap, turns a trades site into a record of real jobs. That needs layouts built around crawlspace finds, not a template.

Touring and doing session drumming out of Nashville before fifteen years in digital marketing is not the usual way into running an agency. Does fitting into someone else's song still shape how you handle client work?
Congrats on being ranked a 2026 top web design company in Chicago.
Saw the Jimmie Johnson site you built, showing him as an investor and team owner and not only as the seven-time champion.
